entities.name: Left atrial myxoma
observations: A left atrial myxoma can cause intermittent functional mitral obstruction, dyspnea, orthopnea, crackles, chest discomfort, and a soft mid-diastolic apical murmur.
Atrial myxoma may produce constitutional symptoms including intermittent fever and fatigue, often through cytokine signaling such as IL-6.
An early diastolic tumor plop is a characteristic, sometimes positional, finding caused by a mobile tumor approaching or prolapsing through the mitral valve.

entities.name: Myxoma tumor plop
observations: The early diastolic extra sound is a tumor plop, an uncommon but discriminating auscultatory finding of atrial myxoma; it may vary with position.

entities.name: Myxoma constitutional syndrome
observations: In a 112-case series, constitutional symptoms occurred in 34% and obstruction-related symptoms in 67% of cardiac myxoma patients.

entities.name: Subacute bacterial endocarditis
observations: Subacute bacterial endocarditis can cause prolonged fever and fatigue but does not explain a tumor plop or intermittent pseudo-mitral-stenosis physiology as well as atrial myxoma.

entities.name: Rheumatic mitral stenosis
observations: Rheumatic mitral stenosis can cause dyspnea and a mid-diastolic murmur but usually produces a fixed opening snap and rumbling murmur rather than a mobile tumor plop.
